INTERNAL MEMORANDUM

Ref: MECH/MEMO/2026/031
Date: 12-03-2026
From: Area Maintenance Engineer, Crude Distillation Unit
To: Head of Mechanical Maintenance
Subject: Repeated mechanical seal failures on crude charge pumps P-2105A/B

1. Pump P-2105A has had three mechanical seal failures in the last eight months (July 2025, November 2025 and February 2026). P-2105B, the standby pump, has had one failure (December 2025).

2. Root cause analysis of the February 2026 failure found misalignment of 0.18 mm between pump and motor, well above the 0.05 mm allowed for this pump. Vibration before the failure was 5.9 mm/s, in Zone C as per SOP-MECH-004.

chunks.text:
## 1. Purpose

To standardise the format of internal approval notes and to state who may approve expenditure of different values.
chunks.source: SOP-ADM-002 Approval Notes and Delegation of Powers.md

chunks.text:
## 2. Standard Format of an Approval Note

Every approval note must contain the following sections, in this order:

1. Subject: one line stating what approval is sought.
2. Reference: inspection report numbers, earlier correspondence, SOP clauses.
3. Background: the situation in brief, with equipment tag numbers.
4. Findings: the key facts and measured values that justify the proposal.
5. Proposal: exactly what is proposed to be done, and by when.
6. Financial implication: estimated cost (in ₹), budget head, and whether it is within budget.
7. Approval sought: the specific approval, addressed to the competent authority as per Section 3.

The note is signed by the initiating officer and recommended by the Department Head before it goes to the approving authority.
chunks.source: SOP-ADM-002 Approval Notes and Delegation of Powers.md
chunks.section: 2. Standard Format of an Approval Note

chunks.text:
## 3. Delegation of Financial Powers (Revenue Expenditure, Maintenance)

Up to ₹5,00,000 (5 lakh): Department Head.
Above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹25,00,000 (25 lakh): General Manager of the department.
Above ₹25 lakh and up to ₹1,00,00,000 (1 crore): Executive Director (Operations).
Above ₹1 crore: Director (Refineries).

Emergency work required to protect safety of people or plant may be started with the approval of the General Manager regardless of value, with post-facto approval of the competent authority within 7 days.
chunks.source: SOP-ADM-002 Approval Notes and Delegation of Powers.md
chunks.section: 3. Delegation of Financial Powers (Revenue Expenditure, Maintenance)

chunks.text:
## 4. Language and Style

Approval notes should be brief, factual and written in the third person. Every measured value must state its unit and source document. Opinions must be clearly separated from facts.

# SOP-INSP-011: Ultrasonic Thickness Inspection of Pressure Vessels

SAMPLE DOCUMENT — fictional "Sample Refinery Ltd." — created for demonstrating the Sovereign Workbench prototype only. Values are illustrative and must not be used for real equipment.

Revision: 2 | Effective date: 15-06-2025 | Owner: Inspection Department
chunks.section: SOP-INSP-011: Ultrasonic Thickness Inspection of Pressure Vessels

chunks.text:
## 1. Purpose

To define the method for ultrasonic thickness (UT) measurement of pressure vessel shells and heads, the calculation of corrosion rate and remaining life, and the fixing of the next inspection date.

## 2. Measurement Method

Thickness is measured with a calibrated digital UT gauge at the fixed Condition Monitoring Locations (CMLs) marked on the vessel inspection drawing. At each CML, three readings are taken and the LOWEST value is recorded. The gauge calibration must be verified on a reference block before and after the survey.

## 3. Key Definitions

Original thickness (t_original): the nominal thickness at the time of construction, from the vessel data sheet.
Minimum required thickness (t_min): the thickness needed to safely hold the design pressure, from the vessel data sheet or design calculation.
Actual thickness (t_actual): the lowest thickness measured in the current survey.

## 4. Corrosion Rate Calculation

Long-term corrosion rate (mm/year) = (t_original − t_actual) ÷ years in service.

If a previous survey is available, the short-term corrosion rate = (t_previous − t_actual) ÷ years between surveys. The HIGHER of the long-term and short-term rates must be used.

## 5. Remaining Life Calculation

Remaining life (years) = (t_actual − t_min) ÷ corrosion rate.

## 6. Next Inspection Date

The next internal or UT inspection must be carried out within HALF of the remaining life, or 10 years, whichever is LESS.

Example: if remaining life is 6 years, the next inspection is due within 3 years.

## 7. Acceptance and Escalation

If t_actual is greater than t_min, the vessel is fit for continued service until the next inspection date.
If remaining life is less than 4 years, the Inspection Engineer must raise an approval note for repair or replacement planning in the next turnaround.
If t_actual is equal to or less than t_min, the vessel must be taken out of service and a fitness-for-service assessment carried out before restart.

## 8. Records

The UT survey sheet, calculations and the next inspection date are entered in the equipment history file. The Inspection Engineer signs the survey sheet; the Head of Inspection approves the next inspection date.

# SOP-MECH-004: Condition Monitoring of Centrifugal Pumps

SAMPLE DOCUMENT — fictional "Sample Refinery Ltd." — created for demonstrating the Sovereign Workbench prototype only. Values are illustrative and must not be used for real equipment.

Revision: 3 | Effective date: 01-04-2026 | Owner: Mechanical Maintenance Department
chunks.section: SOP-MECH-004: Condition Monitoring of Centrifugal Pumps

chunks.text:
## 1. Purpose

This procedure defines how the vibration and bearing temperature of centrifugal pumps are measured, how readings are classified, and what action must be taken when limits are exceeded.

## 2. Scope

Applies to all centrifugal pumps with driver rating between 15 kW and 300 kW in process units, offsites and utilities. Pumps above 300 kW are covered by SOP-MECH-005.

## 3. Responsibilities

The Condition Monitoring (CM) Engineer collects readings, enters them in the CM register and raises a notification when a limit is exceeded. The Area Maintenance Engineer plans the corrective work. The Unit Shift In-charge must be informed immediately of any Zone D reading.

## 4. Measurement Frequency

Critical pumps (marked "C" in the equipment register): readings every 15 days.
Essential pumps (marked "E"): readings every 30 days.
General pumps (marked "G"): readings every 60 days.
After any overhaul, readings must be taken within 24 hours of restart and again after 7 days.

## 5. Vibration Severity Zones

Overall vibration velocity is measured in mm/s RMS on both the drive-end (DE) and non-drive-end (NDE) bearing housings, in horizontal, vertical and axial directions. The HIGHEST of all readings is used for classification.

Zone A (up to 2.8 mm/s): Good. Newly commissioned machines normally fall in this zone. No action.
Zone B (above 2.8 and up to 4.5 mm/s): Acceptable for unrestricted long-term operation. Continue normal monitoring.
Zone C (above 4.5 and up to 7.1 mm/s): Not acceptable for long-term operation. Increase monitoring to weekly, carry out spectrum analysis to find the cause, and plan corrective maintenance within 30 days.
Zone D (above 7.1 mm/s): Danger. Vibration may cause damage. Inform the Shift In-charge immediately, change over to the standby pump, and stop the pump within 24 hours.

## 6. Bearing Temperature Limits

Bearing housing temperature is measured with a calibrated contact thermometer or infrared gun.

Normal: up to 80 °C.
Alarm: above 80 °C and up to 90 °C. Check lubrication (oil level, oil condition, grease quantity) and re-measure within 8 hours.
Trip / stop: above 90 °C. Change over to the standby pump and stop the pump.

A temperature rise of more than 15 °C compared with the previous reading at similar load must be investigated even if the absolute value is below 80 °C.

## 7. Corrective Actions

Common causes of high vibration are unbalance, misalignment, bearing wear, looseness, cavitation and pipe strain. The spectrum analysis report must identify the most likely cause before parts are ordered. Bearing replacement must be done together with a laser alignment check of the pump-motor coupling. After any corrective work the pump must return to Zone A or Zone B.

## 8. Records

All readings, spectrum reports and corrective actions are recorded in the CM register and in the maintenance management system against the equipment tag number. Records are retained for 10 years.

# SOP-SAFE-007: Hot Work Permit

SAMPLE DOCUMENT — fictional "Sample Refinery Ltd." — created for demonstrating the Sovereign Workbench prototype only. Values are illustrative.
Revision: 4 | Effective date: 10-02-2026 | Owner: Fire and Safety Department

# 1. Purpose

To control any work that produces a flame, spark or heat high enough to ignite flammable material, such as welding, gas cutting, grinding and drilling with non-spark-proof tools, inside the refinery battery limits.

# 2. Who Issues the Permit

The permit is issued by the Area Shift In-charge (issuer) to the Job Executing Engineer (receiver). A Fire and Safety officer must countersign every hot work permit inside hazardous areas.

# 3. Gas Test Before Work

A gas test must be done with a calibrated multi-gas detector immediately before work starts and repeated every 2 hours during the work. Work may start only if all of the following limits are met:

Parameter | Acceptable limit
Flammable gas (LEL) | 0 % LEL
Oxygen | 19.5 % to 23.5 %
Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) | Below 1 ppm
Carbon monoxide (CO) | Below 25 ppm

# 4. Precautions

All drains and sewers within 15 metres must be covered with wet gunny bags. A fire watcher with a fire extinguisher must be present throughout the work and for 30 minutes after it ends. Equipment must be isolated with blinds (not only valves) and depressurised.

# 5. Validity

A hot work permit is valid for one shift only (maximum 8 hours) and must be renewed for the next shift after a fresh gas test. The permit must be displayed at the work site.
